key_insight: Classical two-point flux finite volume schemes lose their nominal second-order accuracy when the heat equation has a measure-valued source, with convergence reduced by source singularity and spatial dimension.
engineering_relevance: For simulations with point sources or other singular loads, engineers should expect lower spatial accuracy and choose discretization and mesh strategies accordingly.
method: Extend prior convergence analysis from finite elements to finite volume discretization.
Study the classical two-point flux form for a time-dependent diffusion-reaction/heat equation with measure-valued forcing.
Compare theoretical convergence rates with computational tests using a Dirac delta point source.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports analytical convergence results and computational tests that match the predicted degradation, with order reduced to 1 in 2D and 0.5 in 3D.
watch_item: Accuracy can drop sharply near singular sources, so naive refinement may not recover second-order behavior without specialized treatment.
paper_title: Finite Volume Convergence for a Heat Equation with a Measure-Valued Source
